pr_title: Add support for F# `Async<'T>` as an awaitable type in minimal APIs
pr_body:
Fixes #46773.

- Add support for F# `Async<'T>` as an awaitable type in minimal APIs endpoints using the same `CoercedAwaitableInfo` helper that is used to provide such support for controller action methods.
- Remove extra boxing/unboxing from the `ObjectMethodExecutorFSharpSupport` implementation so that it can be used both for the existing controller action method scenario as well as for the minimal APIs endpoint scenario.
- Add request delegate factory tests for F# `Async<'T>` wherever there were existing tests for `Task<TResult>` or `ValueTask<TResult>`.
- Update the existing F# async coercion to turn `Async<unit>`[^1] into void-returning (non-generic) `Task` instead of `Task<unit>`.
- Add conversion of `Task<unit>` to `Task` and `ValueTask<unit>` to `ValueTask`.
- Add tests showing that the above conversions are supported for runtime request delegate creation but not by the compile-time source generator.

[^1]: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/unit-type

@captainsafia I don't see any existing explicit tests for the OpenAPI generator's treatment of return-type metadata derived from awaitable-returning request delegates other than this:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/7c8a4db4d1019bf716e04cf3b782c76297872156/src/OpenApi/test/OpenApiGeneratorTests.cs#L172-L185

Is it worth adding some? Even if not, should I add a test that shows the coercer's treatment of `Async<unit>`, i.e., that it converts it to `Task<unit>` instead of non-generic/"`void`-returning" `Task`?[^1]

[^1]: It would be nice if we could change that behavior, but neither of these options seems terribly viable:
    1. Change it for both controller actions and minimal APIs endpoints. This could theoretically be a breaking change in behavior for controller actions, since we'd be returning no body instead of the serialized value of `unit` (`null`).
    2. Change it only for minimal APIs endpoints. This would not be a breaking change, but it would introduce a new inconsistency in the treatment of F# `Async<'T>`-returning controller methods and request delegates.

    Making either change would also raise the question of whether the same should be done for `Task<unit>`, to which the answer is likely no.

But if this is uncommon, I feel like we should just create a breaking change announcement and suggest returning `Async<string>/Task<string>/ValueTask<string>` instead of `Async<unit>/Task<unit>/ValueTask<unit>` if you want the "null" serialization.

issue_context.title: Support F# `Async<'T>` as an awaitable type in minimal APIs
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

The F# `Async<'T>` type is [supported as an awaitable return type](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/d1e184bef07ff58d9c093403d583a296d2e73c1c/src/Shared/ObjectMethodExecutor/ObjectMethodExecutorFSharpSupport.cs#L26) for ASP.NET Core controller methods, but not for endpoints added via the `.Map*` minimal APIs extension methods.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I'd like to be able to return F# async values and have them awaited when using minimal APIs endpoints just as I can for controller action methods.

### Examples

- Basic controller example:

    ```fsharp
    type MyController () =
        inherit ControllerBase ()
        // The framework automatically awaits the async value.
        [<HttpGet>]
        member _.Get () = async { return [1 .. 10] }
    ```

- Minimal APIs example:
    
    ```fsharp
    // This does not await.
    app.MapGet ("/", Func<Async<int list>> (fun () -> async { return [1 .. 10] }))
    ```

    ```fsharp
    // Converting the F# async value to a task is required.
    app.MapGet ("/", Func<Task<int list>> (fun () -> async { return [1 .. 10] } |> Async.StartAsTask))
    ```

### Additional context

I can perform the conversion myself using code like this:

```fsharp
open System
open System.Linq.Expressions
open System.Threading
open System.Threading.Tasks

let taskify (f : Delegate) =
    if isNull f then
        nullArg (nameof f)

    let meth = f.Method
    let returnTy = meth.ReturnType
    if returnTy.IsGenericType && returnTy.GetGenericTypeDefinition () = typedefof<Async<_>> then
        let resultTy = returnTy.GetGenericArguments () |> Array.exactlyOne
        let parameters = [| for param in meth.GetParameters () -> Expression.Parameter (param.ParameterType, param.Name) |]
        let lambda =
            Expression.Lambda
                (
                    Expression.Call
                        (
                            (typeof<Async>.GetMethod (nameof Async.StartAsTask)).MakeGenericMethod resultTy,
                            Expression.Invoke
                                (
                                    Expression.Constant f,
                                    box parameters :?> Expression array
                                ),
                            Expression.MakeMemberAccess (null, typeof<TaskCreationOptions option>.GetProperty (nameof None)),
                            Expression.MakeMemberAccess (null, typeof<CancellationToken option>.GetProperty (nameof None))
                        ),
                    parameters
                )

        lambda.Compile ()
    else
        f

let d = Func<_, _> (fun (i : int) -> async { return i })
((taskify d :?> Func<int, Task<int>>).Invoke 3).Result
```

But if I do so, I lose metadata from the original delegate, including parameter names, which affects the generated Swagger/Open API definition, among other things.
comments: Unfortunately ```Async``` is a language specific type in F#. I don't think we could take a dependency on that.

> Unfortunately `Async` is a language specific type in F#. I don't think we could take a dependency on that.

Yes, although it is already [supported in the framework dynamically](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/d1e184bef07ff58d9c093403d583a296d2e73c1c/src/Shared/ObjectMethodExecutor/ObjectMethodExecutorFSharpSupport.cs#L26) for controller action methods.

Why not just use task { ... } directly?
Why not just create a set of overloads for async and call StartAsTask inside?

My experience with minimal apis and F# is that you need a dedicated set of Func overloads anyway or else you have to littler your code with explicit Func annotations everywhere
Triage: We think we might've missed adding support for this scenario and would welcome any PRs!
